Class PythonConversion

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.context.python.PythonConversion
@Internal public final class PythonConversion extends Object
Conversion of Python values to Java: none checks, scalars, collections, optionals, enums and the generated wrapper types.

Maintainer notes. The public methods are called by generated bridge code (see PythonStubGenerator) on every value that crosses from Python to Java, so they sit on the hot path: keep them free of meta-object lookups and string formatting. The package-private methods are the per-type converters PythonCoercion and convertValue(Value, Class) dispatch to. Every converter follows the same rules: None converts to null (or an empty Optional), a value that is already a host object of the target type is returned as is, a generated wrapper (ValueCoercible) is unwrapped rather than copied, and a conversion that cannot be done is an exception, never an empty result, so a bad element does not silently shrink a collection.

Since:
5.2.0

  • Method Details

    • isNone

      public static boolean isNone(@Nullable org.graalvm.polyglot.Value value)
      Returns whether the value represents Java null or Python None.

      Python None is an interop null, so Value.isNull() is the complete check. This method is on the hot path of every bridge call and conversion, so it must not touch the meta object or the string representation of the value.

      Parameters:
      value - The polyglot value
      Returns:
      Whether the value represents Java null or Python None

    • convertValue

      public static <T> @Nullable T convertValue(org.graalvm.polyglot.Value value, Class<T> targetType)
      Generic value conversion method that handles primitives and recursively converts collections.

      The attempts run in this order, and the order matters: a host object that is a ValueCoercible proxy is unwrapped first (a generated wrapper that went through Python must come back as the same Java object, not a copy); a host object of the target type is returned as is; a Java enum target is resolved from the Python enum's name or value; a mapped wrapper type (TargetTypeMapping) is resolved through the wrapper registry; and only then does Value.as(Class) run, which handles primitives, strings and the collection types by GraalPy's own rules.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The target type
      Parameters:
      value - The source polyglot value
      targetType - The target Java type
      Returns:
      The converted value or null
